claims.statement: The Commission's guidance makes nearby heat demand, distance, seasonal variation, financing, risk, and profit relevant to data-centre waste-heat feasibility. That creates a plausible founder wedge in signed site and offtake options plus a standardized evidence room, although enforceability and operator acceptance are untested.

A newly planned or substantially refurbished data centre above the specified energy threshold faces an installation-level cost-benefit analysis and, where feasible, waste-heat use. A missing nearby heat sink can therefore delay a credible plan or strand saleable heat, but the monetary delay cost is project-specific.

The payer hypothesis is a data-centre developer or operator using site-development, engineering, or energy budget at planning/refurbishment, with district-heating utilities or greenhouse operators as possible co-payers. The Commission expects EU data-centre capacity to triple by 2035 and requires reporting, but no buyer has confirmed a brokerage budget.

contrary_evidence: Waste heat can be low-temperature, seasonal, and too distant from a solvent heat sink to be economical.
Large engineering consultancies and district-heating utilities may already originate these projects and control operator relationships.

economics.acquisition_route: Build a GIS screen of Polish substations, planned compute sites, district-heat networks, greenhouses, pools, and industrial heat loads; secure 6-12 month conditional exclusivity from one heat sink before offering a paid pre-feasibility packet to operators.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A proprietary book of optioned heat sinks can earn origination fees, success fees, and small long-term heat royalties across Central Europe; the path becomes substantial only if options are contractible and projects close repeatedly.
economics.founder_time: About 12-18 hours per week for mapping, outreach, and analyst work; licensed engineers produce technical studies per project.
economics.gross_margin_basis: High margin on data-room and origination fees, with external engineering passed through; long-cycle business-development cost is the main margin risk.
economics.payback: Recover mapping and option-acquisition cost from the first paid pre-feasibility mandate, and avoid funding pipes or heat pumps.
economics.pricing: Paid screening and evidence-room fee, milestone success fee at signed offtake, and optional low-single-digit share of contracted heat value.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Transactions are episodic, but each option portfolio and standardized diligence package can serve multiple operators and expansion phases.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Exclusive local heat-sink options, geospatial feasibility data, and closed-project contracting templates
fingerprint.customer: Data-centre developers and operators, district-heating utilities, and stable commercial heat users
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Direct origination through municipalities, utilities, engineering firms, and land or heat-use counterparties
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Option-backed waste-heat origination and pre-feasibility marketplace earning fees and project royalties
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Developer pays at site planning or major refurbishment; success fee is paid when an offtake or connection closes
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A data-centre plan must demonstrate whether economically justified local waste-heat use is feasible

founder_fit: Geospatial screening and project ranking reward analytical work and AI leverage.
The family energy-business context provides vocabulary and contractor adjacency without requiring the founder to build infrastructure.
Capital can stay limited to rights acquisition and evidence until a developer funds engineering.
risks: Site and heat-demand information may be confidential or arrive too late to influence project design.
Exclusive heat-sink options may be legally weak or unattractive to municipalities.
Sales cycles can exceed the founder's runway and require intensive senior relationships.

structure.control_point: A time-limited exclusive mandate over a qualified nearby heat sink and its diligence data room
structure.critical_dependency: Economically matchable year-round heat demand close enough to a planned data-centre site

thesis: Backcast from an EU compute build-out where waste heat must be productively matched: acquire the scarce local heat-sink rights before the data-centre design freezes, then sell an option-backed route to feasibility instead of generic consulting.
title: Waste-Heat Rights Exchange
uncertainties: The number and location of addressable Polish data-centre projects above the relevant threshold are not yet mapped.
Heat-sink owners' willingness to grant exclusivity without upfront payment is unknown.
A developer has not confirmed that an option-backed packet shortens permitting, financing, or design work.
